title: dynamic capture probe and epochal fallback for interleaved decode stability
creator: Caleb Huang
description:
Background: We continue to see transient capture failures and silent replay mismatches when running heterogeneous, interleaved decodes on shared GPU plates under burst load. Root causes are frequently a combination of (a) occupancy variance across streams, (b) preemption and partial warmup windows, and (c) opportunistic kernel selection changes between capture and replay. These manifest as elevated capture_fail_rate during bursts and intermittent correctness regressions that are hard to reproduce.

Goal: Implement a low-overhead dynamic capture probing mechanism and an epochal fallback policy that reduces capture instability and ensures deterministic replay correctness without substantially increasing latency or token cost. The solution should gracefully fall back to conservative capture modes or serial decode when probes indicate instability, and continuously adapt probe aggressiveness based on observed success rates.

High-level approach:
- Probe mode: For a small fraction of inflight prefill windows, run a short capture-probe sequence that records a lightweight signature of the capture (kernel selection, kernel parameters, buffer offsets, and per-layer small checksums of KV slices). Probes must be fast and not record full snapshots.
- Epochal scoring: Maintain an epoch score per worker/GPU that aggregates probe success/failure signals, replay checksums, and capture timeouts. Epoch scores decay over time and determine aggressiveness of capture strategies.
- Fallback policy: If epoch score drops below threshold, switch that worker into a conservative capture mode: longer warmup, per-stream single-threaded capture, or forced kernel pinning. If failures continue, route requests off the worker or fall back to non-cuda-graph decode paths.
- Deterministic replay validation: During probe capture success, compute mini-checksums at critical KV checkpoints and validate them at replay time. On checksum mismatch, mark epoch as degraded and trigger fallback, and emit diagnostic trace for post-mortem.
- Low overhead telemetry: Emit capture_probe_latency_ms, capture_probe_success, replay_checksum_mismatch, epoch_score, and probe_coverage_ratio. These are used for gating rollout.

Design constraints and non-goals:
- Non-goal: This ticket is not building a full binary snapshot rollback system. It is focused on lightweight probes and policies to avoid wide-scale incorrect replays.
- Constraint: Any added latency per request must be minimal; probes should be sampled (e.g., <0.5% of prefill requests by default) and adaptive.

Tradeoffs considered:
- Aggressive probing increases signal but risks extra overhead. We will start conservative and ramp via controlled rollout.
- Checksum coverage vs cost: Use per-layer truncated checksums to balance cost and diagnostic value.

Acceptance criteria:
- Capture probe coverage can be tuned and observed in Console metrics.
- Probe sampling default set to 0.25% and adjustable by runtime flag.
- During synthetic burst tests, capture_fail_rate on probe-enabled workers is reduced by at least 60% compared to baseline when fallback is allowed.
- Any replay checksum mismatch must trigger an automatic epoch downgrade and logging with enough context to reproduce (trace id, kernel hints, sample inputs).
- Latency P50 overhead for non-probed requests remains <= 0.5ms over baseline; probed request P95 increase acceptable up to 5ms.

Implementation plan:
1) Instrument lightweight probe capture point in capture manager to record kernel hints, short KV checksums, and capture timing. (owner: Priya)
2) Implement epoch scorer service local to each worker that aggregates probe signals and applies decay policy. (owner: Jonas Keller)
3) Add conservative capture strategies: forced kernel pinning, extended warmup samples, and single-stream capture path. (owner: Aisha Martinez)
4) Integrate deterministic micro-checksum validation in replay path and tie into epoch scorer. (owner: Priya)
5) Add telemetry and Console dashboard panels for capture_probe_*, epoch_score, and automated alerts. (owner: SRE/Observability)
6) QA: run stress harness with heterogenous sequence lengths, priority preemption, and simulated kernel selection jitter. Validate metrics and rollback triggers. (owner: Test Eng)
7) Canary: roll to 5% of capacity with probe sampling at 0.25%, monitor for regressions, then ramp to 50% when stable.

Monitoring and rollback criteria:
- Immediate rollback if: replay_checksum_mismatch rate > 0.05% of total responses for 15m or capture_fail_rate increases by >25% relative to baseline.
- Auto-degrade policy: if epoch_score remains low across >30m for a worker, traffic is automatically shunted off that worker to protect correctness.

Rollout plan:
- Feature gate behind runtime flag and tenant-level opt-in.
- Canary stage: 5% traffic, 72h observation window.
- Ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 50% over 2 weeks contingent on metrics.

Metrics to collect (SLO/alerts):
- capture_probe_coverage_ratio (goal 0.25%)
- capture_probe_success_rate (goal >99.5% during stable operation)
- capture_fail_rate (trend should decrease)
- replay_checksum_mismatch_count and ratio
- epoch_score_distribution across workers
- end-to-end latency P50/P95 for probed vs non-probed

Security and compliance:
- No secrets are captured by probes. Checksums are truncated and salted to avoid leaking model weights or sensitive content.
- security_review_required: false by default for probing; if tenant opts in to deeper diagnostics, require review.

Notes on reproducibility:
- Probes will record a minimal set of deterministic inputs (seeded RNG state, kernel hints, KV slice ranges). These are sufficient to reproduce capture/replay in a local harness without full sequence logs.

Estimated effort: 8 points across 3 engineers + 1 SRE for observability.
acceptance_criteria: Probe sampling adjustable and visible in Console
60% reduction in capture_fail_rate in synthetic burst tests when fallback enabled
Replay checksum mismatch triggers epoch downgrade and diagnostic logging
design_notes: We will implement per-layer truncated XXHash32 of KV slices taken at prefill boundaries. Kernel hints include selected kernel id, occupancy hint, and launch dimensions. Epoch scorer is a simple EWMA with floor/ceiling clamping and hysteresis to avoid thrash.
test_plan: Unit tests for probe serialization and checksum logic. Integration tests in stress harness: run at least 24h of mixed-length sequences with simulated preemption and verify capture_fail_rate and replay checksums. Fuzz harness to mutate kernel hint ordering and ensure fallback triggers.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Caleb Huang: initial write-up and spike results attached. Spike shows probe overhead of ~1.8ms on probed prefill samples at 10% sampling.
2026-02-27 - Aisha Martinez: design review notes - prefer EWMA epoch scorer with 10min decay, and add a hysteresis window to avoid flip-flopping capture modes.
2026-03-03 - Jonas Keller: implemented local epoch scorer prototype; observed noisy scores under steady burst; reduced sampling to 0.25% fixed in prototype and variance improved.
2026-03-09 - Priya Nair: integrate truncated checksum into replay path; initial mismatch cases all turned out to be kernel-selection drift; added a forced kernel pin path as immediate mitigation.
2026-03-10 - SRE: dashboard panels added to staging; alert thresholds drafted. Next: run full 24h stress with preemption toggled on.
